title: Model Redundancy / Multi-Provider Failover
summary: Continue eligible model work through independent providers without silently changing capability, privacy, or output contracts.
overview: Model redundancy keeps alternative inference capacity available when a primary model endpoint cannot satisfy a request. A failover policy combines availability evidence with compatibility requirements: context length, structured output, tool calling, modality, residency, and evaluated task quality. Two endpoints backed by the same underlying region or upstream dependency may share the same outage.

Failover is a new inference attempt, not the continuation of an interchangeable function. Provider-specific adapters normalize transport and usage data, while a capability registry determines whether the replacement is acceptable. A partially streamed answer, model-generated tool call, or externally executed action requires an explicit restart boundary.

production.poc: A proof of concept can test a secondary model against recorded examples and demonstrate a manual endpoint switch.
production.production: Production adds deadline-aware retries, capability contracts, separate credentials, and clear behavior for interrupted streams.
production.scale: Enterprise scale requires reserved fallback capacity, dependency maps, provider-specific data policies, and regular exercises that run real workloads on the secondary path.

components.name: Capability registry
components.role: Records model limits, supported features, approved data classes, and evaluation versions.

components.name: Routing gateway
components.role: Selects only eligible destinations and preserves the logical request identifier.

components.name: Provider adapters
components.role: Translate schemas, errors, cancellation signals, and token-usage responses.

components.name: Health and quota monitor
components.role: Tracks recent failures, saturation, and available fallback headroom.

components.name: Output validator
components.role: Applies the same business acceptance criteria after any model switch.

flow.title: Resolve constraints
flow.description: Classify the request data and required features before choosing a primary or fallback provider.

flow.title: Reserve attempt budget
flow.description: Divide the remaining deadline between connection, generation, validation, and any permitted alternative attempt.

flow.title: Call primary
flow.description: Record provider, model revision, input policy, and attempt identifier with the inference span.

flow.title: Classify interruption
flow.description: Distinguish throttling or transport failure from invalid input, policy rejection, and already-visible output.

flow.title: Select compatible fallback
flow.description: Check independent capacity and replay the request only when its privacy and capability contract remains valid.

flow.title: Validate and disclose
flow.description: Check the result against the task contract and record the provider transition for operations and cost attribution.

diagrams.caption: An outage does not authorize a provider that falls outside the original request contract.

diagrams.title: Failover after an interrupted attempt
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant G as Model gateway
 participant P as Primary provider
 participant C as Capability registry
 participant S as Secondary provider
 G->>P: Attempt within deadline
 P-->>G: Retryable failure before accepted output
 G->>C: Check fallback eligibility
 C-->>G: Approved compatible route
 G->>S: New attempt with remaining budget
 S-->>G: Candidate result
 G->>G: Validate before acceptance
diagrams.caption: A secondary attempt has its own budget and validation while retaining the logical request identity.

useCase.title: Claims document extraction during provider disruption
useCase.situation: A claims intake service extracts structured fields from uploaded repair estimates throughout the business day.
useCase.problem: The primary inference region becomes unavailable while claim submissions continue.
useCase.requirement: Maintain intake while preserving document residency and the approved extraction schema.
useCase.architecture: A gateway maintains two evaluated extraction models, a regional policy registry, and a durable pending queue.
runtime: The first attempt fails before a result is accepted.
The gateway checks regional eligibility, submits to the secondary model, and validates totals and required fields.
useCase.failure: If the secondary cannot process a document modality or has exhausted quota, the claim remains queued with a visible processing state.
useCase.impact: Measure completion delay, fallback quality, and queued age separately; service continuity is useful only if the extracted fields remain reliable.

tradeoffs.cost: Cold or under-tested fallback capacity may be unavailable during an incident.
Adds contract, adapter, and evaluation maintenance.
Reduce the set of requests eligible for immediate failover.

failures.detection: Secondary throttling rises as primary traffic transfers.
failures.recovery: Shed optional tasks and place eligible requests in a bounded durable queue.

failures.detection: Schema validation fails despite a successful HTTP response.
failures.recovery: Reject the output and route to an approved simpler workflow.

mistakes.fix: Retry infrastructure failures selectively; do not bypass policy or authorization denials.
Restart a visible answer cleanly or expose an explicit interruption state.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming two brands mean independent failure domains
mistakes.fix: Map actual infrastructure and upstream dependencies.

whenToUse: Use for inference services with material availability requirements.
Use where at least two models meet a measured task-quality floor.
Choose it when eligible workloads can tolerate a bounded replay delay.
whenNotToUse: Avoid unapproved cross-region transfer of sensitive prompts.
Avoid failover for tool effects whose completion is still ambiguous.
Do not promise identical reasoning or output across unrelated models.
checklist: Evaluate secondary models on production task slices.
Reserve fallback quota or document queue behavior.
Record provider and model on every accepted result.
